purpose: ExtraMarkups adds two custom MRML markups node types to 3D Slicer: a "Label" node that draws an arrow with a text label, and a "Shape" node that draws primitive/parametric shapes (sphere, ring, disk, tube, cone, cylinder, arc, ellipsoid, toroid, etc.) from control points placed in slice and 3D views. It targets Slicer users who want annotated, scene-persistable geometric markup objects; both modules are hidden and expose their options inside the Markups module.
summary: Pure C++/VTK/MRML extension with no Python, no network, no downloads, no shell or file-system writes beyond Slicer's own storage nodes; nothing malicious or AI-directed found. Catalog entry is consistent (build_dependencies [] vs EXTENSION_DEPENDS "NA", branch revision supported) and CMake lists every source it builds. License is CeCILL-B (permissive, distribution allowed), though source headers say BSD-3-Clause. Main issues are ordinary robustness bugs: a JumpToPoint observer on the display node is never removed (dangling clientData if the display node outlives the node), the shape type is unconditionally reset to Sphere when a node is added to the scene, and an invalid shape name from JSON leaves the node in an inconsistent state. No tests or sample data.

safety.rationale: Searched the whole tree for system/popen/QProcess/QNetwork/curl/socket/exec/eval and for file removal or rename: only documentation URLs matched. The code is C++ MRML/VTK widget code that reads and writes only through Slicer's own JSON storage nodes (Label/MRML/vtkMRMLMarkupsLabelJsonStorageNode.cxx, Shape/MRML/vtkMRMLMarkupsShapeJsonStorageNode.cxx); no telemetry, credentials, downloads or obfuscation, and no text aimed at reviewers.

environment.rationale: No Python, pip, PyTorch or package installation anywhere; the extension is built by CMake against Slicer libraries only (CMakeLists.txt:17-23, Label/CMakeLists.txt:36-42). No global side effects at import/startup beyond registering the two markups node types and options widgets in the Markups factory (Label/qSlicerLabelModule.cxx:119-126).

packaging.rationale: CMakeLists.txt adds both subdirectories and each kit lists its sources; the UI files referenced by Label/Widgets/CMakeLists.txt:22-24 and Shape/Widgets/CMakeLists.txt:22-24 exist on disk, as do the icons referenced by the .qrc files. EXTENSION_DEPENDS "NA" matches the entry's empty build_dependencies, and the entry's branch revision "main" is supported by policy. Only cosmetic leftovers (unused *OptionsWidget.ui files, VTKWidgets kits built with SlicerMacroBuildModuleLogic) were found.

license.rationale: LICENSE.txt is the full CeCILL-B v1.0 text, which explicitly grants distribution rights (Article 5.3, LICENSE.txt:213-223), and README.md:16 states the work is licensed under CeCILL-B. Source headers carry BSD-3-Clause notices from BWH/Oslo University Hospital; both are permissive, so distribution is permitted, but the two notices are inconsistent.

soundness.rationale: Read the module, logic, MRML node and storage-node sources. The design follows Slicer conventions (hidden modules, options widgets in the Markups factory, JSON storage nodes, MRMLNodeModifyBlocker), but vtkMRMLMarkupsShapeNode adds an observer to its display node and never removes it, and vtkSlicerShapeLogic::OnMRMLSceneNodeAdded unconditionally forces the shape to Sphere, which can silently change a node's shape.

utility.rationale: README.md plus per-module READMEs with screenshots document the two node types and the shape variants, and the modules are tier 3. There are no tests, no sample data, no clinical-use disclaimer, and both modules are filed under the 'Testing.TestCases' category (Label/qSlicerLabelModule.cxx:109), which makes them hard to discover.

findings.title: JumpToPoint observer on the display node is never removed, leaving a dangling clientData pointer
findings.explanation: The callback command stores the markups node as clientData and is registered on the display node. The destructor (lines 59-63) removes only OnPointPositionUndefinedCallback from the node itself: `this->RemoveObserver(this->OnPointPositionUndefinedCallback);`. The display node keeps its own reference to the command, so if the display node outlives the markups node (shared/retained display node, scene-close ordering, node replaced while the display node stays in the scene), a later JumpToPointEvent invokes OnJumpToPoint with a freed node pointer, i.e. a use-after-free crash in Slicer. The same asymmetry exists when the display node is swapped: the guard `!OnPointPositionUndefinedCallback && !OnJumpToPointCallback` prevents re-attaching the observer to the new display node.
findings.suggestion: Store the observed display node and remove the JumpToPoint observer in the destructor and whenever the display node changes (e.g. in a SetAndObserveDisplayNode override), mirroring the existing RemoveObserver call for OnPointPositionUndefinedCallback.

findings.title: Every shape node added to the scene is forced to Sphere, discarding its shape type
findings.explanation: OnMRMLSceneNodeAdded runs for every vtkMRMLMarkupsShapeNode added to the scene, not only for freshly created ones. A node produced by copy/paste or duplication (CopyContent then add to scene) or by a script that sets a shape before adding the node is silently converted to a Sphere, and the user's chosen geometry is lost. Because ShapeName has no vtkSetMacro/XML serialization, the shape type is only persisted through the JSON storage node, so any path that restores a node without that storage node also falls back to Sphere.
findings.suggestion: Only apply the default when the node still has the uninitialised value (ShapeName == ShapeName_Last), or move the default into the node constructor instead of the scene-added callback.

findings.title: SetShapeName stores the new value before validating it, so an unknown name leaves the node inconsistent
findings.explanation: GetShapeNameFromString returns -1 for an unknown string (lines 151-168), and the JSON storage node passes that straight to SetShapeName (Shape/MRML/vtkMRMLMarkupsShapeJsonStorageNode.cxx:90). SetShapeName assigns ShapeName = -1 first and then hits `default : vtkErrorMacro("Unknown shape."); return;` (lines 325-327), so the node ends up with ShapeName == -1 while RequiredNumberOfControlPoints/MaximumNumberOfControlPoints and the measurements still describe the previous shape. GetShapeNameAsString(-1) then returns an empty string, which is written back on the next save.
findings.suggestion: Validate the incoming value before assigning (reject negative values), and have the storage node ignore an unknown shape name instead of applying it.

findings.title: Label and Shape widget headers share the same include guard
findings.explanation: Shape/VTKWidgets/vtkSlicerShapeWidget.h:21-22 uses the identical guard `__vtkslicerslicingcontourwidget_h_`. Any translation unit that includes both headers (for example a future module or test that uses both widgets) silently loses the second class declaration and fails to compile with confusing errors. The same copy-paste also produced `void operator=(const vtkSlicerLabelWidget) = delete;` (line 49) with a by-value parameter instead of a reference.
findings.suggestion: Give each header a unique guard (e.g. __vtkSlicerLabelWidget_h_ / __vtkSlicerShapeWidget_h_) and fix the deleted assignment operator signature.

findings.title: GenerateUniqueColor dereferences the scene without a null check and can index past the colour table
findings.explanation: GetMRMLScene() can return nullptr (the same function checks it in RegisterNodes and OnMRMLSceneNodeAdded), but here it is dereferenced unconditionally, so a call during scene teardown would crash. In addition, `colorTable->GetColor(this->NextColorIndex, rgba)` is called before the wrap-around check, so when NextColorIndex equals GetNumberOfColors() the lookup fails and the previous rgba value is reused. The identical code is duplicated in Shape/Logic/vtkSlicerShapeLogic.cxx:135-156.
findings.suggestion: Guard against a null scene and clamp/wrap NextColorIndex before calling GetColor; consider sharing one implementation between the two logic classes.

findings.title: Unused UI files and VTKWidgets kits built with the Logic macro
findings.explanation: Label/Widgets/Resources/UI/qMRMLMarkupsLabelOptionsWidget.ui and Shape/Widgets/Resources/UI/qMRMLMarkupsShapeOptionsWidget.ui are committed but not referenced by any CMakeLists, so they are dead files. Separately, Label/VTKWidgets/CMakeLists.txt:29 and Shape/VTKWidgets/CMakeLists.txt:29 use SlicerMacroBuildModuleLogic to build the VTKWidgets kits instead of SlicerMacroBuildModuleVTKWidgets; this builds today but deviates from the Slicer template and may not set up the kit the way Slicer expects.
findings.suggestion: Remove the unused .ui files and switch the VTKWidgets kits to SlicerMacroBuildModuleVTKWidgets.

findings.title: License file says CeCILL-B while source headers say BSD-3-Clause
findings.evidence: This work, as a whole, is licensed under the terms of the [CeCILL-B](http://cecill.info/licences/Licence_CeCILL-B_V1-en.txt) free software license agreement (BSD style).
findings.explanation: LICENSE.txt contains the CeCILL-B v1.0 text, but most source files carry the Slicer template header 'Distributed under the OSI-approved BSD 3-Clause License' (e.g. Label/VTKWidgets/vtkSlicerLabelRepresentation2D.h:3) and 'Portions (c) Copyright Brigham and Women's Hospital (BWH)' (Label/qSlicerLabelModule.h:5). Both licenses permit redistribution, so this is not a distribution blocker, but users cannot tell which terms apply to which file.
findings.suggestion: State the licensing per file or directory in the README (e.g. CeCILL-B for the author's code, BSD-3-Clause for files derived from the Slicer template).

findings.title: No tests, sample data or clinical-use disclaimer; modules hidden under Testing.TestCases
findings.explanation: Both modules report the 'Testing.TestCases' category (Shape/qSlicerShapeModule.cxx:107-110) and are hidden (isHidden() returns true), so users only find them through the Markups module's options widget. The repository contains no test directory and no sample scene, and the READMEs give no statement about suitability for clinical measurement, even though the Shape node computes lengths, areas and volumes that a user might read as measurements.
findings.suggestion: Add a short disclaimer about measurement accuracy/clinical use, provide a sample scene or test data, and consider a more descriptive category than Testing.TestCases.

not_checked: Shape/MRML/vtkMRMLMarkupsShapeNode.cxx is 65 KB; I read only lines 1-400, so the measurement, reslice, spline and parametric code paths (including any WriteXML/ReadXML overrides) were not reviewed.

The large representation and widget sources were not read: Shape/VTKWidgets/vtkSlicerShapeRepresentation2D.cxx (64 KB), vtkSlicerShapeRepresentation3D.cxx (54 KB), Shape/Widgets/qMRMLMarkupsShapeWidget.cxx (33 KB), Label/VTKWidgets/vtkSlicerLabelRepresentation2D.cxx, vtkSlicerLabelRepresentation3D.c
The .qrc resource files, the .ui files and the PNG icons/screenshots were not opened (binary or not inspected), so I cannot confirm every icon path referenced by the .qrc files resolves.
I could not build the extension or run it in Slicer, so build success on any platform and the runtime behaviour of the observers are unverified.

The catalog entry pins scm_revision "main" (a moving branch); I reviewed the snapshot provided for commit f5c833befbd67d8e58f0103c1efffa594c66dc93 and did not verify what the current branch tip contains.
No CI build/test reports were available to me.
questions_for_author: Is the JumpToPoint observer on the display node intentionally left in place when the markups node is destroyed, or should it be removed like OnPointPositionUndefinedCallback?
Why does vtkSlicerShapeLogic::OnMRMLSceneNodeAdded force SetShapeName(Sphere) for every shape node added to the scene rather than only for newly created nodes?
Which license governs which files: CeCILL-B (LICENSE.txt) or BSD-3-Clause (the Slicer template headers in most sources)?
